_description: Parts catalog for the ChiMesh v0 build — 3 solar-powered RAK4631 Meshtastic nodes for proof-of-mesh in Chicago. Prices on 'core' parts are per node; 'consumable' parts are shared across all nodes; 'tools' are one-time and excluded from the build estimate. All parts are compatibility-checked end-to-end: Solar panel (5V) -> TP5000 (LFP-configured) -> LiFePO4 cell -> JST-PHR-2 on RAK19003 -> RAK4631 -> IPEX -> SMA pigtail -> 915 MHz SMA antenna. CRITICAL: do NOT charge an LFP cell through the RAK19003 USB-C port; its onboard charger is Li-ion only (4.2 V termination) and will overcharge LFP (3.65 V max). See ChiMesh.md §6.1 for the safe re-flash workflow.
pricesNote: Per-node estimates in USD. Tools and consumables are shared / one-time and excluded from the per-node total. Verify via the Google Shopping link on each card before ordering.

categories.core: Required for every node — one of each per node.
categories.consumable: Shared across all 3 nodes — order one kit.
categories.tools: One-time tools. You may already own these; the build estimate excludes them.

parts.name: RAK4631 WisBlock Core (nRF52840 + SX1262 LoRa)
parts.note: The brain. Nordic nRF52840 MCU with Semtech SX1262 LoRa radio on one module. Listens at ~8–12 mA combined (SX1262 RX ~4.6 mA + nRF52840 active ~3–6 mA), vs ~17 mA for Heltec V3 — that delta is what makes solar viable in Chicago winter. See §6.3 for the full budget. Make sure you get the 915 MHz US variant, not the 868 MHz EU variant.

specs.label: Radio
specs.value: Semtech SX1262 LoRa, up to +22 dBm

specs.label: Frequency
specs.value: 915 MHz (US) — pick correct SKU for region

specs.label: Sleep
specs.value: ~3 µA System OFF, ~7 µA w/ RAM retain

parts.name: RAK19003 WisBlock Mini Base Board
parts.note: Carrier board for the RAK4631. Adds USB-C (for flashing only — do NOT use to charge LFP), JST-PHR-2 battery connector, and IPEX antenna pass-through. The Mini variant is the smallest base and fits inside a 100x68x50mm enclosure with room for the cell and panel cable.

parts.name: LiFePO4 18650 Cell (IFR18650, ~1500 mAh)
parts.note: MUST be LiFePO4 (LFP / IFR18650), NOT Li-ion. Chicago winters charge below 0°C; Li-ion plates lithium permanently in those conditions and kills the cell in one winter. LFP charges safely to ~-10°C and lasts 2000-5000 cycles vs 500-1000 for Li-ion. Half the mAh in the same form factor is the price of admission.

parts.name: Single 18650 Battery Holder with Leads
parts.note: Plain plastic single-cell holder with pre-soldered red/black wires. Get the 'with leads' variant, not the PCB-mount type — you need wires you can crimp into the JST-PHR-2 connector on the RAK19003.

parts.name: TP5000 Solar Charge Controller (LFP-configurable)
parts.note: CRITICAL: this board has a jumper that selects between Li-ion (4.2 V termination) and LFP (3.6 V termination). Set it for LFP before connecting. Stock charge controllers in cheap solar lamps are tuned for Li-ion and will damage an LFP cell — that is why we bypass anything that came with the panel and use this module instead. Solar panel goes to this module's IN+/IN-; LFP cell connects to its BAT+/BAT-; the BAT output then feeds the RAK19003 JST-PHR-2 directly.

specs.label: Input
specs.value: 4.5–8 V DC (5 V solar panel fits)

specs.label: Chemistry
specs.value: Li-ion 4.2 V OR LFP 3.6 V via jumper

specs.label: MPPT
specs.value: No (linear) — fine for 2 W class panels

parts.name: 5V / 2W Monocrystalline Solar Panel (~110 x 80 mm)
parts.note: Sized for the Chicago winter floor: ~150-200 mAh/day harvest in December assuming 1.5 peak sun hours and a slightly dirty panel face. Summer harvests 3-5x more, plenty of margin. Open-circuit voltage ~6.5 V, MPP ~5 V; pairs cleanly with the TP5000 input range. Output wires usually bare — terminate into the TP5000 IN+/IN- screw terminal or solder.

parts.name: 915 MHz SMA Antenna (~5 dBi rubber duck)
parts.note: Must be SMA (not RP-SMA). Match the frequency to your region — 915 MHz for US/AU, 868 MHz for EU, 920–925 MHz for AS923. A 5 dBi whip gives the best size-vs-range tradeoff for proof-of-mesh; upgrade to a fiberglass colinear (8+ dBi) later if you put a node on a rooftop. Antenna stays vertical for matching polarization with the rest of the Meshtastic network.

parts.name: IPEX (u.FL) to SMA Pigtail, ~10 cm
parts.note: The RAK4631 has an IPEX (u.FL) antenna footprint; this cable adapts it to a standard SMA bulkhead through the enclosure wall. Get the female-SMA-bulkhead version (panel-mount nut) so it threads through the hole you drill in the case. RG178 coax is standard; 100-150 mm is the right length for a 100 mm box. WARNING: SMA and RP-SMA look identical but are NOT interchangeable. Buy SMA (used for LoRa); RP-SMA is for WiFi/Helium. RAK's own 'u-fl-to-rp-sma-cable' is RP-SMA — do not use it here. Adafruit #851 is SMA (correct); Adafruit #852 is RP-SMA (wrong).

specs.label: End B
specs.value: SMA female bulkhead w/ panel nut

parts.name: IP65 ABS Weatherproof Junction Box (~100 x 68 x 50 mm)
parts.note: Cheap clear or grey ABS box from any hardware site. IP65 is enough for a vertical wall mount; if you flat-mount it skyward, look for IP66+. Internal volume fits the RAK19003 + Mini base + 18650 holder + TP5000 + slack cable. Drill one hole on top/side for the antenna SMA bulkhead and one on the bottom for the panel cable gland.

parts.name: M12 IP68 Cable Gland (for solar panel pass-through)
parts.note: Threaded gland that seals around the solar panel's output cable as it enters the enclosure. M12 fits a small drilled hole; M16 if you have a thicker cable. Skip if you'd rather use silicone sealant in a smaller hole, but the gland is reusable when you swap parts.

parts.name: JST-PHR-2 connectors + 22 AWG silicone wire + M3 screws
parts.note: Shared across all 3 nodes — order one kit. JST-PHR-2 male housings + crimp terminals connect the battery holder leads to the RAK19003. 22 AWG silicone-jacket wire handles all low-voltage hops cleanly. M3x6 / M3x8 screws + double-sided VHB foam tape mount the panel and board to the enclosure interior.

specs.label: JST
specs.value: PHR-2 housings + crimp pins (2.0 mm pitch)

specs.label: Wire
specs.value: 22 AWG silicone, red + black, ~3 m each

specs.label: Tape
specs.value: 3M VHB or generic foam, ~25 mm wide

parts.name: Heat-shrink tubing assortment (2-8 mm)
parts.note: Shared across all 3 nodes. Use 2-4 mm for individual solder joints (panel leads, cell leads), 6-8 mm for the JST pigtail bundle. Black is fine; coloured packs help differentiate red/black joints visually.

parts.name: 60/40 rosin-core solder, 0.8 mm
parts.note: Shared across all 3 nodes (and probably your next 30 projects). 0.8 mm is the right diameter for the small pads on the TP5000 and RAK19003. Skip lead-free unless you specifically want to — 60/40 leaded flows easier and is forgiving for hand-soldering.

parts.name: Temperature-controlled soldering iron
parts.note: Any temperature-controlled iron is fine. A Pinecil V2 or a Hakko FX-888D handles every joint in this build. The cheap fixed-temperature 'pencil' irons work too but tend to burn pads on the small SMD pads of the TP5000 / RAK19003 — go controlled if you can.

parts.name: Digital multimeter
parts.note: Used during troubleshooting to verify cell voltage (3.2-3.65 V on a healthy LFP), panel open-circuit voltage (~6.5 V Voc), and TP5000 output. Any cheap DMM works — even a $15 Harbor Freight model is enough for DC volts in this range. Auto-ranging is convenient but not required.

parts.name: Wire strippers + flush cutters
parts.note: Strippers sized for 20-24 AWG handle the 22 AWG silicone wire cleanly. Flush cutters (also called diagonal cutters or 'snips') trim component leads and zip-tie ends without nicking adjacent wire. Often sold as a combo pair.

parts.name: JST crimp tool (for PHR-2 terminals)
parts.note: Optional but recommended. A proper crimp on a JST-PHR-2 terminal is far more reliable than a pliers-squashed one and is what you want for an outdoor unattended node. Generic 'IWS-3220M' or 'Engineer PA-09' work fine. Alternative: buy pre-crimped JST pigtails on Amazon and skip this tool entirely.

parts.name: Heat gun (mini) or lighter
parts.note: Shrinks heat-shrink tubing over solder joints. A mini USB-C heat gun is overkill and great; a $2 lighter also works for one-off joints. Hair dryer is too cool to shrink most polyolefin tubing.

parts.name: Drill + bits (6 mm + 12 mm step or twist)
parts.note: For drilling the enclosure: 6 mm hole for the SMA bulkhead nut, 12 mm hole for the M12 cable gland. A cordless drill + a metric bit set covers both; a step bit ('unibit') makes cleaner holes in plastic. If you have neither, a soldering iron melted carefully through ABS works in a pinch (do it outdoors — fumes).

parts.name: Phillips #1 screwdriver
parts.note: Most IP65 enclosure lids use 4x M3 or 4x #4 Phillips screws. Any small Phillips driver works.
